executive_summary.narrative:
66 hypotheses tested, 17 proven and reported. Unproven candidates are in the raw artifacts, not shown as findings.

Multiple proven vulnerabilities—particularly Remote Code Execution, multiple SQL/LDAP injection flaws, and critical authentication bypasses—pose immediate threats to system availability, confidentiality, and integrity. These high-severity exploits represent clear paths to persistent compromise and should be addressed above all others. Given the deterministic nature of our testing results, we advise urgent patching and hardening of authentication pipelines and unprotected APIs. Immediate mitigation steps will significantly reduce exposure, followed by architectural improvements to prevent recurrence.

findings.title: Remote Code Execution via Unauthenticated API Endpoint
findings.recommendation: An attacker can execute arbitrary code on the server, leading to full system compromise and data theft. Immediately restrict access to the `/api/Quantitys/` endpoint by enforcing strong authentication and authorization checks. Audit all related backend logic for potential command injection points. Conduct a full security review of the API layer.

evidence.note: VERDICT: PROVEN — The endpoint discloses internal resource details such as product quantities and user limits.

findings.title: Account Takeover via SQL Injection
findings.recommendation: Attackers can fully compromise user accounts, including admin accounts, leading to unauthorized access and potential data breaches. Sanitize and validate all user inputs, especially the `email` parameter in the login API. Use prepared statements or ORM features to prevent SQL injection. Implement account lockout mechanisms and monitor for unusual login attempts.

findings.title: LDAP Injection in Login Mechanism
findings.recommendation: Enables attackers to bypass LDAP-based authentication or query internal directory structures, compromising enterprise identity systems. Replace dynamic LDAP query construction with safe APIs or parameter binding. Log and monitor failed authentication patterns. Harden directory service permissions and limit query scope wherever possible.

findings.title: Authentication Bypass on Quantity Management API
findings.recommendation: Unauthenticated users can access and potentially modify sensitive product and inventory data, risking data integrity and regulatory compliance issues. Implement robust API-level authentication for `/api/Quantitys/`, including token validation, session checks, and access control lists. Remove or disable unnecessary public endpoints.

findings.title: Admin Configuration Exposure Without Authentication
findings.recommendation: Critical internal configurations may be leaked, enabling deeper system exploitation and lateral movement. Enforce strict role-based access control (RBAC) for administrative endpoints like `/rest/admin/application-configuration`. Protect them with multi-factor authentication (MFA) where applicable.
